reason: All engineered inputs are directly stored per-event/per-jet branches: jet_pt/eta/phi/mass/energy (up to N jets), jet_sophonAK4_probB/probC/probL (continuous), HT, pass_selection, pass_4j3b_selection, pass_4j2b_selection, jet_hadronFlavor/partonFlavor. No adapter needed; standard flattening/padding of jet arrays into a fixed-width feature vector is a data-engineering step, not a provenance gap.

Same stored feature set as XGBoost baseline (jet kinematics + continuous SophonAK4 scores + event-level HT/flags); a dense network consumes the same flattened/padded representation. No missing branches.

Per-jet kinematics (jet_pt/eta/phi/mass) are stored and sufficient for the assignment network's inputs, but the required TRUTH jet-to-Higgs assignment label is not directly stored as a branch. Only gen_bhadron_fromhh (boolean "is this b-hadron from any Higgs in the decay chain", no h1-vs-h2 index) and the two truth Higgs 4-vectors (gen_higgs1_*, gen_higgs2_*) are stored. A deterministic offline adapter -- deltaR-match reconstructed jets to fromhh==1 gen_bhadron entries, then assign the resulting jet pairs to h1 vs h2 by minimizing combinatorial deltaR/mass distance to (gen_higgs1_p4, gen_higgs2_p4) -- can construct unambiguous assignment labels for HH signal samples (gghh_kl0/1/5, vbf_*, training_signal_h3var). This adapter is not yet built or validated in this audit. QCD/ttbar events have no genuine Higgs truth (gen_higgs1/2 undefined) and are correctly out of scope for assignment-label training.

Assignment head has the same requirement and same adapter dependency as native SPA-Net above. The second head (event classification / mass regression) is READY_NOW on its own: gen_dihiggs_mass, gen_higgs1_mass, gen_higgs2_mass, and process_index are already stored as direct truth labels requiring no adapter. Overall status is gated by the assignment head.

Full PF-candidate constituent set is stored: part_px/py/pz/energy (4-vectors), part_charge, part_pid, part_d0val/d0err/dzval/dzerr (impact parameters), part_dr/deta/dphi (relative kinematics), and part_label (AK4-jet membership index) / part_fjlabel (fatjet membership index). This is sufficient to build genuine pairwise attention (e.g. deltaR_ij, m_ij pairwise features computed from the stored 4-vectors) rather than a jet-level-only network. No adapter needed for the raw inputs themselves; the architecture (attention that is actually modified by pairwise kinematic features, not just per-token concatenation) is an implementation choice, not a data gap.

Constituent-level inputs for training the upstream ParT embedding model are READY_NOW (see pairwise_aware_ParT row). However: (1) no pretrained "general-purpose ParT embedding" checkpoint exists in this repository -- only the pretrained SophonAK4/Sophon flavor taggers and the 138-class jet-free classifier ensemble, which are not generic embeddings -- so the ParT embedding model itself must be trained first inside Track B before it can be frozen; (2) SPA-Net's assignment-head truth-label adapter (see native_SPA_Net row) is still required. Status reflects both dependencies, neither of which is blocked, both of which require deterministic construction before use.

Track B provides the generic raw constituent ingredients a JEPA-style particle encoder would need (four-vectors, charge, PID, impact parameters, jet membership -- identical to the ParT row). JP-JEPA itself, however, is not part of this repository or the associated paper; its exact input contract (feature list, normalization, masking convention) is defined elsewhere (Track A / external JP-JEPA documentation) and was NOT verified against Track B's schema in this audit. Status is conditional: constituent-level readiness is confirmed, but confirmation that Track B's specific branch set matches JP-JEPA's actual expected input contract is an open action item outside Track B's scope. SPA-Net's assignment-label adapter dependency also applies.
